clue.text: Try this Ampleforth product

indicators.note: a product is what something yields, so the run of letters is produced by the two words written together

parts.note: the last letter of the first word runs on into the start of the school's name

explanation.surface: An advert inviting you to taste something made at Ampleforth, the Yorkshire monastery and school.
explanation.walkthrough: Ampleforth is a Benedictine abbey and boarding school in Yorkshire; the monks really do sell their produce, which makes the surface convincing.
explanation.definitionFit: A sample is a small portion offered so that people can taste or test it before buying.

clue.text: Fair Sally's seated in jaunting-car

definitions.note: the clue gives the first half of the fairground name Aunt Sally; the answer is the word that precedes Sally

indicators.note: something seated in a vehicle is carried inside it, so the letters sit within the word that follows

parts.note: the letters sit inside the first part of this Irish cart's name

explanation.surface: A girl called Sally, pretty and fair, rides in an Irish jaunting-car.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aunt Sally is a fairground game in which you throw sticks at a dummy's head, so the fair's Sally is the aunt. A jaunting-car is a light two-wheeled Irish horse cart.
explanation.definitionFit: Aunt Sally is the traditional British fairground figure pelted with missiles, so at a fair Sally carries this title.

clue.text: Church elder confused by Peter's introduction of ritual

indicators.note: a confused person has things muddled, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

indicators.note: an introduction comes at the start, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: first letter of ritual

explanation.surface: A senior churchman is baffled when someone named Peter brings a new ritual into the service.
explanation.definitionFit: A presbyter is an elder in the Presbyterian and early Christian churches, an office holder who helps govern a congregation.

clue.text: Land in Spain, say

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)
to say something is to state it

explanation.surface: Someone talks of owning property in Spain, perhaps a villa.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma tempts you to read 'Spain, say' as an example of a country; instead each word gives its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is a large area of land owned by one person or family, usually with a big house.

clue.text: Detectives are aware of these doubts

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the people police believe may have committed a crime
second meaning: a verb, mistrusts or has misgivings about

explanation.surface: Investigators know about these uncertainties in the case.
explanation.definitionFit: As a plural noun the word names people under police suspicion; as a verb it means to distrust or feel unsure of something.

clue.text: Undemanding, unlike a hooker!

definitions.note: split into two words, it describes a forward who plays straight
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read as two words: a rugby hooker is a forward, but hooking means bending the ball or playing crooked

explanation.surface: An exclamation that an easy task is nothing like the work of a prostitute.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby the hooker is one of the forwards; to hook is also to send a ball curving in golf or cricket, and a hooker is slang for a prostitute, so an honest forward is not one.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uncomplicated and easy to do is described as plain and direct; read as two words it is an honest player in the pack.

clue.text: Locums try to do this at the dentist

definitions.meaning: first meaning: temporary substitutes filling a post

definitions.text: try to do this at the dentist
definitions.note: a verb phrase: read as two words, filling holes in teeth
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read as two words: plugging holes, as a dentist fills cavities

explanation.surface: Stand-in doctors attempt something during a visit to the dentist.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a doctor covering for an absent colleague, a temporary fill-in; a dentist's job is closing cavities in teeth.

clue.text: Girl found in a chapel, topless

indicators.note: without its top, a down entry loses its first letter

parts.note: a bethel is a nonconformist chapel or seamen's place of worship

explanation.surface: A shocking discovery: a girl without a top in a chapel.
explanation.walkthrough: Bethel, Hebrew for 'house of God', is a name used for Methodist and Baptist chapels, especially in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethel is a girl's first name, so it stands for any girl in crossword convention.

clue.text: They are used when giving a 22

definitions.text: They are used when giving a 22

parts.words: They are used when giving a 22
parts.note: surface reading: something handed over along with entry 22, apparently an inventor
setter's reading: 22 is a word for a call, and giving someone one is ringing them up

explanation.surface: Things employed when presenting the item at 22.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer at 22 is BELL; 'give me a bell' is British slang for phone me, and Bell also invented the device.
explanation.definitionFit: These devices are what you ring someone on, and Alexander Graham Bell is credited with inventing them.

clue.text: He planted a tree using these hollow acorns

indicators.note: to use material is to work it into something new, so the letters are worked into a fresh order
something hollow has had its insides scooped out, leaving only the shell of the word before

parts.note: the outside letters of these
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone grew an oak from empty acorns.
explanation.walkthrough: The tree is a family tree, not an oak; the man who started the line planted it.
explanation.definitionFit: A forebear at the root of a family line is figuratively the planter of its genealogical tree.

clue.text: Put off when nearly through

definitions.meaning: first meaning: postponed, suspended for now

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase describing a waiting caller
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a telephone caller waiting to be connected

explanation.surface: Something postponed just as it was almost finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Through' means connected on the phone, not finished.
explanation.definitionFit: A deferred plan is left pending; a caller waiting with music before being connected is in the same suspended state.

clue.text: They indicate the stakes, not the mistakes

definitions.text: They indicate the stakes, not the mistakes

parts.words: They indicate the stakes, not the mistakes
parts.note: surface reading: something that shows what is at risk rather than the errors made
setter's reading: the papers carry a word that can also mean errors, but here they record wagers at the bookmaker

explanation.surface: Documents that show what is at risk rather than the blunders made.
explanation.walkthrough: A slip can be a small error or a small piece of paper; at a bookmaker's the paper records your bet.
explanation.definitionFit: These paper forms record a punter's wager and stake at a bookmaker's shop, and they are a kind of small slip.

clue.text: It makes perfect tribute on radio

indicators.note: radio carries only sound, so the word is identified by how it is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a tribute is praise, a word heard identically to its near-twin

explanation.surface: A broadcast tribute that rounds off a programme perfectly.
explanation.walkthrough: Compliment (praise, with an i) and complement (completing part, with an e) sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A complement is the thing that completes a whole, such as a full crew or the angle that makes up ninety degrees.

clue.text: A gunrunner

parts.note: surface reading: a smuggler of illegal weapons
setter's reading: split in two, a firearm brand that is also a racing animal

explanation.walkthrough: 'Gunrunner' looks like an arms smuggler, but split it into gun and runner: one word is both a revolver make and a young horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Colt is the American firearms maker famous for its revolvers, and a young male horse that may race is called the same.

clue.text: Famous racehorse who lit up the Classics?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the 1933 Derby winner and leading sire
second meaning: the Titan of light in Greek myth

explanation.walkthrough: The Classics are both the great British flat races, which the horse won, and classical literature, where the Titan is father of the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyperion won the Derby and St Leger in 1933, and in Greek mythology he is the Titan father of Helios, Selene and Eos.

clue.text: Sun-god in rage brings nasty weather

parts.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god
taken as written
to storm is to rage

explanation.surface: An angry sun god whips up bad weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like it puts one piece inside another, but here it is simply its own two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy downpour accompanied by wind is a kind of unpleasant meteorological event.

clue.text: Popular colours

definitions.note: an adjective in the sense of usual or widely adopted

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a flag or banner, as in a regiment's colours

explanation.walkthrough: Colours here is the regiment's flag, not paint shades.
explanation.definitionFit: A widely used, typical model is described this way; a military flag carried into battle is also known by the same word.

clue.text: Opening shot before the starter's orders

definitions.text: Opening shot before the starter's orders

parts.words: Opening shot before the starter's orders
parts.note: surface reading: a starting pistol fired at a race meeting before the start is called
setter's reading: the first course is ordered, and a shot is a drink taken before it

explanation.surface: A pistol going off at the beginning of a race, before the starter has given the signal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under starter's orders' is racing language, but here the starter is the first course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: This drink is taken before a meal to whet the appetite, ahead of the first course being served.

clue.text: Roman law pursues one prickly family

indicators.note: to pursue is to follow behind, so the first-mentioned piece comes after the second

parts.note: Roman numeral one
lex is Latin for law

explanation.surface: Roman justice hunts down a single family of awkward people.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilex is the botanical genus of hollies, plants known for their spiny-edged leaves.

clue.text: Find fault with square boxes

definitions.meaning: second meaning: clean blows, as a box on the ear is a cuff

explanation.surface: Someone complains about the shape of cardboard containers.
explanation.walkthrough: Boxes here are blows, as in a box on the ears, not containers.
explanation.definitionFit: To criticise something is informally to rubbish it, and hard punches landed squarely are also called by this word.

clue.text: They are fingered in exchange, connecting calls

definitions.text: They are fingered in exchange, connecting calls

parts.words: They are fingered in exchange, connecting calls
parts.note: surface reading: an old telephone exchange where operators put calls through
setter's reading: placed on fingers as vows are swapped at a marriage service

explanation.surface: Switchboard operators handling equipment at a telephone exchange to connect callers.
explanation.walkthrough: The exchange is of vows, and the calls are rings, a word for both phone calls and bands of gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Marriage bands are put on fingers when a couple exchange vows, and they bind two people together.

clue.text: Some say Alexandra made it suitable for the Prince of Wales, for instance

definitions.text: it suitable for the Prince of Wales, for instance

indicators.note: some of the spoken words, a portion only, contains the letters needed

parts.note: the end of the name runs on into the first letters of the next word

explanation.surface: Some claim Princess Alexandra made something fit for the heir to the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: The Prince of Wales is a West End theatre in London, not the royal heir; 'made' lends its first letters as well as reading as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A play is the kind of thing staged at a London playhouse such as this one.

clue.text: Inventor of the bottomless pot

indicators.note: with no bottom, a down entry loses its last letter

parts.note: a pot is a paunch, a big stomach

explanation.surface: The person who came up with a pot with no base.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Graham Bell is credited as the inventor of the telephone.

clue.text: State with Bartok in and playing around

indicators.note: the actress sits inside the other letters
the played-about letters go round the outside
playing about with something rearranges it freely

parts.note: taken as written
Eva Bartok was a Hungarian-born film actress

explanation.surface: A US state where the composer Bartok's music is being performed.
explanation.walkthrough: Bartok suggests the composer Bela, but the setter wants the 1950s film star Eva Bartok.
explanation.definitionFit: Nevada is one of the fifty United States, in the American west, home to Las Vegas.

clue.text: Fast in the water …

parts.note: surface reading: speedy when swimming or sailing
setter's reading: fixed firmly, as a moored ship is held

explanation.surface: Something quick in the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Fast means firmly fixed, not quick.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship held in place by its heavy hook dropped to the seabed is secured and cannot drift.

clue.text: … and fast on land

parts.note: surface reading: speedy when on the ground rather than at sea
setter's reading: stuck firmly, as a boat run aground is

explanation.surface: Something quick ashore, continuing the previous clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Again fast means stuck, here of a vessel driven onto the shore.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship driven onto the beach or a sandbank is left stuck fast and unable to move off.

clue.text: 5 down in the herb-garden

definitions.note: a phrase standing for a noun: a plant found there
definitions.meaning: second meaning: an old name for a medicinal plant

explanation.surface: An easy thing found among the herbs.
explanation.walkthrough: A simple is an archaic word for a medicinal herb, grown in physic gardens.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means easy and uncomplicated, matching the earlier answer; as a noun it is an old term for a healing plant.
